summary:
For the NASA challenge, our team developed an interactive, gamified space mission designed to bridge the gap between theoretical aerospace concepts and practical mission planning. While students and aspiring engineers often rely solely on textbook formulas, our simulation empowers them to actively visualize, calculate, and experience the complexities of interplanetary travel.
  Based on the engineering frameworks of the 2022 Mars Transportation White Paper and solely on other NASA studies.
   The game challenges players to design and manage a realistic journey to the solar system. Players make critical decisions regarding spacecraft geometry, structural mass, propulsion systems, and strict traveling budgets. By manipulating these variables in real time, users can immediately see how aerodynamic shape and fuel constraints directly impact trajectory, payload capacity, and mission success.
   Ultimately, this project transforms complex orbital mechanics and resource management into an engaging, hands-on learning tool. Whether used in a classroom or by independent space enthusiasts, our game demystifies the logistical hurdles of deep-space exploration and inspires the next generation of engineers to solve the travel challenges.
details:
Our team developed an interactive, gamified space mission simulation that transforms complex aerospace concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. Players design and manage interplanetary journeys to destinations across the Solar System, making decisions about spacecraft geometry, structural mass, propulsion systems, fuel, payload capacity, and mission budgets.
Grounded in the 2022 Mars Transportation White Paper and other NASA scientific studies, the simulation allows users to adjust engineering variables in real time and see how their decisions affect mission feasibility and performance.
Gamification is the core of our project. By combining scientific learning with interactive challenges, decision-making, and experimentation, we make aerospace engineering more accessible and enjoyable while encouraging critical thinking and problem-solving.
Our team prioritized scientific accuracy, realistic engineering constraints, resource management, and user engagement. Ultimately, we aim to inspire the next generation of engineers by making exploration across the solar system both educational and exciting.
